PipelessAPIKeyCredential.title: Pipeless API Key
PipelessAPIKeyCredential.x-credential-instructions: Open Account → Apps in Pipeless and copy your App ID and app API key. Paste the key without the Bearer prefix. Each app has its own key and graph database. NoClick checks the connection by reading recent events for that app.

contentSchema.description: The event to be added.

start_object.description: An object to be written to your data. Only one object can exist for each type + id combo. If any of your write patterns provide an object that doesn't exist, it will be created. If the object already exists, the existing object will be used in your write operation, and if created_on or modified_on differ from the values already associated with the object, those values will be updated.

id.description: The id of your object. The id can be a string (up to 40 characters) containing any number, alpha character, spaces, or the following special characters: @-!#%^&()/+=;:'"?<>\][{}.,

type.description: The type of an object. Can be any one of our predefined types. Although it is flexible what object type you use, as a best practice, we suggest you pick the one that relates best to the data you are representing. Doing this also allows specific algos to automatically work with their default settings.

created_on.description: An optional DateTime string in the format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS in whatever timezone you use. If not set, and the object needs to be created, this value will be set to the current UTC time.

modified_on.description: An optional DateTime string in the format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS in whatever timezone you use. If not set, the value will be set to the same value as created_on.

type.description: The type of relationship for an event. Can be any one of our predefined types. Although it is flexible what relationship type you use, as a best practice, we suggest you pick the one that relates best to the data you are representing. Doing this also allows specific algos to automatically work with their default settings.

created_on.description: An optional DateTime string in the format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS in whatever timezone you use. If not set, and the relationship needs to be created, this value will be set to the current UTC time.

single.description: Whether the relationship can be duplicated or not. If single is true (default), then a relationship of each type can only exist once between the same start and end objects. If false, a relationship of the same type can exist multiple times between the same start and end objects.

end_object.description: An object to be written to your data. Only one object can exist for each type + id combo. If any of your write patterns provide an object that doesn't exist, it will be created. If the object already exists, the existing object will be used in your write operation, and if created_on or modified_on differ from the values already associated with the object, those values will be updated.

id.description: The id of your object. The id can be a string (up to 40 characters) containing any number, alpha character, spaces, or the following special characters: @-!#%^&()/+=;:'"?<>\][{}.,

type.description: The type of an object. Can be any one of our predefined types. Although it is flexible what object type you use, as a best practice, we suggest you pick the one that relates best to the data you are representing. Doing this also allows specific algos to automatically work with their default settings.

created_on.description: An optional DateTime string in the format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS in whatever timezone you use. If not set, and the object needs to be created, this value will be set to the current UTC time.

modified_on.description: An optional DateTime string in the format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS in whatever timezone you use. If not set, the value will be set to the same value as created_on.

synchronous.description: Whether the event should be created asynchronously or synchronously. Default is false (asynchronous). On success, async will return 202 Accepted, sync will return 201 Created.
synchronous.title: Synchronous

PipelessGetActivityActionsFeedConfig.description: Fetch the activity feed for a user (or any other object type). This activity feed format will return acted upon entities as the main result. Ex. one item per post, article, product, etc. Each single item has associated actions. Ex. product a product

contentSchema.description: The object (ex. user) you want to fetch the activity feed for.

id.description: id of the object you want to fetch.

type.description: type of the object you want to fetch.

object.description: The object (ex. user) you want to fetch the activity feed for.
object.title: Object

contentSchema.description: An array of the relationship types that represent the concept of "following" in your data. If none provided, by default the relationship type "followed" will be used.

follow_relationship_types.description: An array of the relationship types that represent the concept of "following" in your data. If none provided, by default the relationship type "followed" will be used.
follow_relationship_types.title: Follow relationship types

contentSchema.description: An array of the object types that can be followed in your dataset and that you want to be used for this activity feed. If none provided, by default any object type that is found based on the allowed follow_relationship_types will be used.

follow_object_types.description: An array of the object types that can be followed in your dataset and that you want to be used for this activity feed. If none provided, by default any object type that is found based on the allowed follow_relationship_types will be used.
follow_object_types.title: Follow object types

contentSchema.description: An array of the relationship types of the actions you want to show up in the activity feed. If none provided, by default any relationships that are present in the resulting feed items will be returned.

event_relationship_types.description: An array of the relationship types of the actions you want to show up in the activity feed. If none provided, by default any relationships that are present in the resulting feed items will be returned.
event_relationship_types.title: Event relationship types

contentSchema.description: An array of the object types that can appear as content in the feed. If none provided, any object type that results from the other settings will be shown in the feed.

event_object_types.description: An array of the object types that can appear as content in the feed. If none provided, any object type that results from the other settings will be shown in the feed.
event_object_types.title: Event object types

exclude_self_object.description: If this value is false (the default), then the user you are fetching the feed for can appear in the feed results as an acting user (if the user follows themself) or action user (object that is being acted on by users the user follows). If set to true, the user the feed is being fetched for will not appear in the results.
exclude_self_object.title: Exclude self object

allow_missing_object.description: If this value is false (the default), then trying to fetch an activity feed for a non-existent object will result in a 404 object not found error being returned. If this value is true, then in the case of a non-existent object, an empty activity feed will be returned with no error.
allow_missing_object.title: Allow missing object

return_cursor_for_events.description: This value defaults to false. When set to true, each returned event will contain an additional property called cursor, which contains the cursor value for that specific item. Just like end_cusror in page_info, any cursor value can be used in the before param to begin pagination after the specified cursor.
return_cursor_for_events.title: Return cursor for events

PipelessGetRecommendedContentConfig.description: Gets recommeneded content for a given object (ex. recommended posts for a user based on their previous actions, collaborative filtering, and tags associated with the content they interacted with).

id.description: id of the object you want to fetch.

type.description: type of the object you want to fetch.

content_object_type.description: The type of object that is being recommended.
content_object_type.title: Content object type

primary_positive_relationship_type.description: The primary positive indicator a user can take on the content type that's being recommended. This should be the action a user can take that you consider most important to indicating that an object appeals to their tastes. If value is not provided, it will default to "liked".
primary_positive_relationship_type.title: Primary positive relationship type

secondary_positive_relationship_type.description: The secondary positive indicator a user can take on the content type that's being recommended. This should be the action a user can take that you consider to be important in indicating that an object appeals to their tastes. It will be weighted less than the primary positive relationship type, but still taken into account. If value is not provided, it will default to "viewed".
secondary_positive_relationship_type.title: Secondary positive relationship type

primary_negative_relationship_type.description: The primary negative action a user can take on the content type. This should be the action a user can take that you consider to be important in indicating that an object does not appeal to their tastes. Content that the user marked with this type will not be returned in recommendation results. If value is not provided, it will default to "disliked".
primary_negative_relationship_type.title: Primary negative relationship type

content_tagged_relationship_type.description: Set this relationship to the relationship you use to set tags on the content that is being recommended. If a value is not provided, "taggedWith" will be used by default.
content_tagged_relationship_type.title: Content tagged relationship type

content_tag_object_type.description: Set this relationship to the object you use for tags on the content that is being recommended. If a value is not provided, "tag" will be used by default.
content_tag_object_type.title: Content tag object type

contentSchema.description: You can use this option to provide some ids of tags you want to contribute to coldstart recommendations if no real recommendations are yet available for a user. If you provide one or more tag ids for this field, trending content from those tags will be used as coldstart recommendations when personalized recommendations are not available.

coldstart_tag_ids.description: You can use this option to provide some ids of tags you want to contribute to coldstart recommendations if no real recommendations are yet available for a user. If you provide one or more tag ids for this field, trending content from those tags will be used as coldstart recommendations when personalized recommendations are not available.
coldstart_tag_ids.title: Coldstart tag ids

contentSchema.description: You can use this option to provide ids of tags that will be used to filter the returned recommended content. If any tag ids are specified in this value, then a piece of recommended content will only be returned if it is tagged (using specified content_tagged_relationship_type) with all of the tags provided in this option.

filter_tag_ids.description: You can use this option to provide ids of tags that will be used to filter the returned recommended content. If any tag ids are specified in this value, then a piece of recommended content will only be returned if it is tagged (using specified content_tagged_relationship_type) with all of the tags provided in this option.
filter_tag_ids.title: Filter tag ids

include_content_authors.description: Default value is false. If set to true, an array called authors will be provided with each item, providing the authors of the recommended content. If this is set to true, then content_created_relationship_type must also be set.
include_content_authors.title: Include content authors

content_created_relationship_type.description: A relationship type that represents a user creating content in your data. Required if include_content_authors or exclude_content_from_followed is set to true.
content_created_relationship_type.title: Content created relationship type

exclude_content_from_followed.description: Default value is false. If set to true, content that was created by authors that the user follows will be excluded. If set to true, content_created_relationship_type must also be set.
exclude_content_from_followed.title: Exclude content from followed

followed_relationship_type.description: A relationship type that represents a user following another user in your data. If exclude_content_from_followed is set to true and this value is not set, then it will default to followed.
followed_relationship_type.title: Followed relationship type

dismissed_relationship_type.description: A relationship type that represents a user dismissing the recommendation of a piece of content in your data. If this param is not provided, it defaults to "dismissed".
dismissed_relationship_type.title: Dismissed relationship type

PipelessGetRecommendedContentConfig.title: PipelessGetRecommendedContentConfig

PipelessGetRecommendedUsersToFollowConfi.description: For a given user (or any object type), get a list of recommended users for the target user to follow, based on their behavior/tastes.

id.description: id of the object you want to fetch.

type.description: type of the object you want to fetch.

followed_relationship_type.description: The relationship type in your data that is used to represent a user (or other type) following someone else. If this value is not provided, it will default to "followed".
followed_relationship_type.title: Followed relationship type

content_created_relationship_type.description: A relationship type that represents a user creating content in your data. If no value is provided, this will default to "posted".
content_created_relationship_type.title: Content created relationship type

positive_relationship_type.description: The positive indicator a user can take on the content type that users can create. This should be the action a user can take that you consider most important to indicating that an object appeals to their tastes. If value is not provided, it will default to "liked".
positive_relationship_type.title: Positive relationship type

content_tagged_relationship_type.description: Set this relationship to the relationship you use to set tags on the content that is created by users. If a value is not provided, "taggedWith" will be used by default.
content_tagged_relationship_type.title: Content tagged relationship type

content_object_type.description: The type of object that represents the content being created by users. If no value is provided, this defaults to "post".
content_object_type.title: Content object type

content_tag_object_type.description: Set this type to the object you use for tags on the content that is created by your users. If a value is not provided, "tag" will be used by default.
content_tag_object_type.title: Content tag object type

dismissed_relationship_type.description: A relationship type that represents a user dismissing the recommendation of a piece of content in your data. If this param is not provided, it defaults to "dismissed".
dismissed_relationship_type.title: Dismissed relationship type

allow_missing_object.description: If this value is false (the default), then trying to fetch an activity feed for a non-existent object will result in a 404 object not found error being returned. If this value is true, then in the case of a non-existent object, an empty activity feed will be returned with no error.
allow_missing_object.title: Allow missing object

PipelessGetRecommendedUsersToFollowConfi.title: PipelessGetRecommendedUsersToFollowConfig

content_published_relationship_type.description: Teh relationship type that represents a user publishing content. If this value is not set, and content tagged relationship type has been set, then this value will default to "posted".
content_published_relationship_type.title: Content published relationship type
